chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of the Iraqis, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Hadrami, from his father, from Uthman ibn Zayd, from Jabir, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Jabir! May Allah not remove you from the shortfall nor the deficiency.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Deficiency or failure to fulfill duties
key_terms.جَابِر: Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, a prominent companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the supplication 'La akhrajaka Allahu min al-naqs wa al-taqseer'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) invokes divine preservation for Jabir ibn Yazid from *al-naqṣ* (inherent deficiency) and *al-taqṣīr* (negligence in duty), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between human finitude and spiritual striving. This supplication underscores the ethical imperative to actively rectify shortcomings rather than accept them as static states, a concept deeply rooted in the Shia understanding of *‘ismah* (infallibility) as the ideal to which the Imams guide the faithful. The context highlights the scholarly tradition of viewing spiritual growth as a dynamic process of overcoming the 'deficiency' mentioned in Chapter 35 of *Al-Kafi*.
